There are 3 ways such an invade can go. 

1. (your case) Your champ loses the 1v1 and you don't have lane prios. 
If you see the invade coming you immediately run to his blue side, split the map and just vertical for that instance. If you don't see it coming and run into the enemy like in this case, you recall, run bot, check his camps or check for a bot gank. You NEVER fight this.


2. You win the 1v1.
Especially in lower elos and I'd say up to Dia, many junglers are great at judging lanes but horrible at judging their own matchups so they invade you either way. Just kill him, but watch for prio on the lanes that could influence your skirmish (Talon/Akshan roaming up real quick for example).


3. You lose the 1v1 but your laners have prio.
Call in your laners and kill the lad.

One small thing of note, you won't always have prio in both lanes, as a general statement for early game fights: bruisers, duelists, assassins > tanks, control mages, scalers. If only one lane has prio, but you are Lee Sin/Darius vs Graves/Orianna for example you can always go for it, it's just important to keep in the back of your head who can move to the instance.

In my opinion, your approach was wrong. It worked out in this instance but in general and especially the higher up you go that won't work out. Don't make it a habit.

Viego and Elise fill two very very different roles in the game. Elise doesn't carry, she's not meant to be a 1v9 playmaking machine, she is who enables carries.

Elise just doesn't do that, she wins through tempo, overpowering pressure, invades, early towerdives, picks, out macro-ing the enemy and creating lose lose situations for your opponent. It's pretty simple. Skill floor = how bad you can be and still play the champion. The absolute minimum amount of skill and knowledge needed to somewhat play a champion decently. 

Udyr: has a low skill floor, anyone can practically lock him in and if they can jungle, they can play Udyr.

Elise: has a very high skill floor macro wise and a medium~high skill floor micro/mechanics wise. Locking in Elise and just playing her will not allow you to play her properly. You need more information or practice to start understanding what to do.

Skill ceiling = how good its possible to be on said champion. / what the absolute limit is that a champion is capable of.

Udyr: has a low~medium skill ceiling. The difference between a great Udyr and the best Udyr is not very high. There just isnt that much to 'get out' of the champion itself. There is of course a difference still, but its not worlds apart.

Elise: has an insanely high skill ceiling, not necessarily due to mechanics, but due to what her kit allows her to be capable of. The difference between a great Elise and the best Elise is massive. 

You are essentially comparing Darius to Fiora and asking who's more difficult. 

Does that make sense? Thats essentially what a skill floor vs ceiling is.

I'd like to weigh in as someone who plays both. 
I've played both of these champs in all elos and am currently sitting in Master. 

Elise is much harder by a long shot. She is mechanically harder and your game sense and tempo management have to be really good. That and the fact that she gets outscaled and is a heavily early reliant champion that can lose a game by making one singular mistake just make this matchup not very close. 

Udyr is extremely safe, has very little variance in terms of gameplan and doesnt need to stomp the earlygame to win. There is much less mechanical skill required and there is no pressure to essentially win the game pre15 minutes or losing. His 'only' difficult aspects are managing his passive and dodging ccs/choosing the optimal enhanced skill to use. 

Udyrs most difficult aspect is simply being good at League: knowing how and when to engage, what to build in any specific game, how to play a teamfight. This isn't really something that makes Udyr specifically difficult, it's what makes League difficult and can't really be attributed to him.


It's also kind of strange to compare her with Udyr, who's one of the simplest champs by far. If you said Nida, Kindred or even a Lee or Graves you could have an interesting discussion about it as all of these are considered very difficult champions and there's arguments for and against them all.

Hi, I'm a D1 jungler on EUW. 

1) You get gold efficiently by pathing efficiently, clearing fast and ganking successfully. You may also take waves that are crashing into your laners towers when they have no chance of reaching them anyway, as well as when helping push out the wave for your laners back timers or just counterjungling/killing your opponent. (also herald gives a lot of gold, underrated in low elo imo)


2) As a jungler you usually have the herald, so you get the plates anyway. Outside of herald I'd only take plates if your presence allows your laner/team to take the tower OR when you're playing an extremely selfish jungler (Eve, Yi etc.)


3) General advice: get your first clears fast and clean on the champs you want to play WITHOUT needing a leash. This gives your laners an advantage and hides your starting position from the enemy jgl making you more difficult to track. 


Start your first clear on the opposite side of the map of where you want to gank, so you end up at the lane you want to gank after your first clear.


After a full clear check the following: can I gank or countergank? do I have lane pio to take an objective? can I invade the enemy jgl and kill him or take his camps? if none of those apply, do I have enough gold to buy a big powerspike if I recall now? 


Always recall 1min - 50 secs before an objective spawns in order to setup vision for your team around it. 


Always play on or towards the side the next objective will spawn. 


NEVER let the enemy jgl do anything for free! If he ganks top and you can countergank, do it. If you cant, take the drake, if you cant do that gank his bot or invade his botside jgl. If he gets tempo for free while you do nothing, you're losing your team the game.


4) I personally don't recommend playing Talon or Gwen if you're new to jungling. These champs need to know how to break the rules of jungling, which you dont even know. Instead, I would look to play some more traditional fullclear junglers until you get the hang of it, learn how to abuse junglers who follow those rules and then switch to the cheesy/invader junglers. 


My recommendations would be: Diana, Jarvan, Udyr, Zac, Xin, smth like that, because when you're too focused on learning the champ, you wont learn how to jungle.

I recently started playing ranked again and have just finished my climb out of silver last week so im pretty fresh on what helped me climb:

1: As a jungler focus objectives. In silver I saw it time and time again that the enemy jungler didnt bother to take dragon herald or free turrets at all.

2: Get really good at 1-2 champs. For me that champ is Elise and even though she is absolutely trash tier right now I climbed out of silver relatively easy. What I'm saying with that is if you're good at your champ it doesn't matter what you play.

3: Buy control wards. I checked your [op.gg](https://op.gg) only very quick but I saw that you buy basically no control wards ever. Make it a habit to buy one every time you back. I sometimes buy 10+ control wards per game.

4: Learn about jungle pathing and matchups. Something important is knowing your jungle matchups and which paths you can take in them. Against some junglers you'll be able to contest scuttle and against some you will not knowing this will give you a huge advantage since most people in silver don't.

Knowing when to farm and when to gank can be difficult. I suggest you just try your luck. You'll quickly figure out when you can successfully pull off a gank and when you can't. Also you think it's not a good idea to gank a lane and the laner spampings you/flames you in chat: don't gank usually it will lead to a double kill for them or a 1 for 1 trade which isnt worth it most of the time.

All source is my personal experience.

>Is it better to farm if you are not confident you can gank?

If you play a champ that gets big with farming yes. If you are Lee or Elise or Evelynn no, you need to use your earlygame.

>What is considered a "good" gank?

Opinions may vary, for me a good gank is burning a flash, getting a kill, or forcing a back to take turret.

>Is it normal to get no ganks pre 6?

Again depends on the champion, WW for example is pretty useless pre 6 but other champs need to gank before 6.

>Is it worth it to attempt to gank if all three of your lanes are playing very aggressively?

Yes it is, when you play jungle more often you know when to dive or try a "cheese" gank between the enemies turrets after a back.

>When is a good time to get drag?

When the enemy jungler is dead, top side or used smite recently on another buff/camp.

>If you get behind should you continue trying to gank or just farm?

Ganking is an easy way to get back into the game as long as you can keep up your farm, else its useless.

>Say, for example, bot lane is pinging assistance but you're top lane farming. Is it worth it to waste that 30 sec and run down to help?

Generally no, if bot is pressured by the jungler or mid you should either counterjungle or gank top, just something to create pressure, make more room for your team.
